name: AI Query Optimisation
title: AI Query Optimisation
answer: Query optimisers choose how a database executes a query, and research and commercial systems now use machine learning to estimate costs, recommend indexes and tune settings automatically. This shifts part of the optimisation workload from hand-written heuristics to models trained on query logs and workload patterns. The risk is that a learned choice is hard to explain when it goes wrong, because the model's reasoning is not visible in the same way as a rule-based plan.

sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: AI query optimisation runs inside or alongside database engines, often as a service that observes query plans and execution statistics. It may use the database's own catalog and statistics tables, plus external model serving endpoints or in-process libraries. For SQL systems, Model Context Protocol servers can expose database schemas and query interfaces to AI tools; this site tracks 262 active MCP servers for SQL databases and warehouses.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work typically starts by collecting query text, execution plans, runtime and cardinality data from the database's logs. Models are trained to predict row counts or execution time for candidate plans, or to choose among index and configuration changes. Some systems use reinforcement learning to adjust database parameters by treating query latency as a reward signal. The learned model then scores candidate plans or settings before the optimiser commits to an execution path.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: A learned optimiser introduces governance questions about why a particular plan was chosen and which model version produced it. Teams often keep the rule-based optimiser as a fallback and record the model identifier, training data range and feature values alongside each query plan. Because the model may learn from sensitive query text, access to training logs and plan repositories needs the same controls as the underlying database. The main risk is that a bad learned estimate causes a regression that is difficult to trace without a clear audit trail.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction is toward optimisers that adapt continuously to changing workloads rather than being retrained in batches. Learned index selection and automatic materialized view choice are likely to become standard parts of database administration. As AI assistants connect to SQL systems through Model Context Protocol servers, query optimisation will also need to handle natural language queries and hybrid relational plus vector search plans.
